newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia says no plans to delink from S.Africa rand.
newsitem.headline: Namibia says no plans to delink from S.Africa rand.

text.p: Nambia's did not plan to delink its currency from the rand as this would remove the benefits it had gained from South Africa's restrictive monetary policy, the central bank said in its 1996 annual report.

"Namibia's membership of the Common Monetary Area (CMA), which has on the whole proved beneficial to the country, necessitates a monetary policy stance that supports the fixed exchange rate between the Namibia dollar and the South African rand," the report, released on Wednesday, said.
The bank said the policy of a fixed exchange rate had been effective in maintaining price stability and a single-digit inflation rate in 1996 of eight percent, compared to 10 percent in 1995.
The bank said this was due to tight monetary policies pursued by the South African Reserve Bank and transmitted to Namibia through a fixed exchange rate.

"This relationship has helped Namibia to achieve inflation rates that are low by regional standards, contributing to the government's long-term objective of growth in a stable macro-economic environment", it said.
The Bank of Namibia has mostly followed the South African Reserve Bank's policies, especially regarding interest rates.
South Africa's Reserve Bank has maintained punitively high interest rates in the country, helping rein in inflation.
In May, South African inflation rose 9.5 percent year-on-year in May, compared with a 9.9 percent increase in April.
